notes.title: Manhattan v2.0 Beta 13 Released
notes.content:
Many thanks to feedback from users; I am pleased to present signiificant update, including basic sample import and a new probability feature, but also many performance and reliability improvements. 

The highlights of this release are:

Basic sample import support
While you wait for the full custom samples and instruments editing features, which are under active development, I've added a basic mechanism to get custom samples into Manhattan. To do so, simply add your samples (e.g. .wav) to the Manhattan project file using a .zip utility. 
   Manhattan's file format is a .zip compatible archive, which contains all the information about your project (principally in the Module.xml file). To do add a sample, take a Manhattan project (.zm file), extract it to a folder, add the sample to that folder, and zip it back up. Alternatively, some utilities will allow you simply to open the archive and add files. To get your system to recognise .zm as a .zip file you can use the "Open with" feature, or rename the extension. 
   This specific feature is designed to teach students about how files, folders, and zips work; the forthcoming instrument editing feature will include full GUI support for the process.

New dice() function for weighted randomness
This new function provides several ways to generate a random number by throwing a die with a given number of sides optionally with specific weights. The function can be used for any purpose, but is designed for indexing arrays (which start at index 0) and makes it easier to implement things like Markov chains. It will generate whole number beginning with 0 up to one less than the number of sides (e.g. 6 sides = 0,1,2,3,4,5), as per the following examples:

dice(6) - generates a random number from 0 to 5, with even weightings.
dice(1,2,1) - generates a random number from 0 to 2, where 1 (the second) is twice as likely.
dice(@array, .volume) - generate a random number by looking at the rows of @array, using the size of the array as the number of sides and its .volume column for their weights.

New code-based data interpolation using "to" operator
You can now easily dynamically interpolate between two values in your pattern using the "to" operator, specifying the range to be affected and then setting the start and end values:

[0 to 9].volume = 0 to 64 - interpolates from silence to full volume over the first nine rows.

Improved Windows 11 support
Windows 11 seems to be more fussy about audio drivers than previous versions, causing some users to experience glitchy audio or none at all. This version includes several workarounds to hopefully ensure robust and smooth audio support - please let me know if you have problems, using the forum.

New Instrument menu with categories
The instrument menu is now sorted by category to aid searching, but also supporting new categories for user-defined samples (see above) and instruments (coming soon).

Improved graphics and UI performance
This version includes some significant optimisations of the graphics code, which means Manhattan is more selective and economical with drawing the UI. Things may feel smoother, not least the Windows' version's splash screen, but fundamentally the lower CPU/GPU usage should translate to better battery life.

--- oOo ---

Please keep the feedback coming and support the project by reviewing Manhattan, liking the videos on YouTube, etc. If this release is well-received, the next will be Release Candidate 1 - but working on custom instruments / samples and multiple patterns is also in the works!

notes.title: Manhattan v2.0 Beta 11 Released
notes.content:
Many thanks to feedback from users on the forum and over email, especially Esa Ruoho (aka "Lackluster"). The product of many months of work, the highlights of this release are:

Independent Playback Threads / Layers
The parallel playback threads feature is now more powerful and intuitive, maintaining their own indendent channel states. Practically, this means that you can now have multiple blocks playing simultaneously on a single channel - where previously they shared a channel so could interfere with each other, which could be used creatively but could also create unexpected results. This should allow you to make even more effective use of pattern space without having to grow your piece sideways.

Embeddable Scores
Manhattan features a score view in the toolbar, but you can now also embed scores in the pattern, using the score() function - just tell it what you want to score, and where you want it to appear and it shall appear and update as the music updates. See the built-in documentation for details.

Numerous UI and Quality of Life Improvements
This release makes myriad tweaks to the user interface and workflow that should make working with Manhattan smoother, more familiar, and faster - including improved support for mouse interaction.

Audio and Graphics Performance Improvements
To better support the new theading engine and in preparation for forthcoming surround sound support, the audio engine has been further optimised to increase performance between 20% and 50% (depending on your system), while also make several improvements to audio quality. A few smaller tweaks to DirectX (Windows) and Cocoa (Mac) graphics code should also see smoother UI animation, with a future support for Apple Metal also in the works.

New Tutorials: Bytes & Pieces
Originally developed for in-person workshops, Bytes + Pieces are a series of fun 'card-based' challenges to quickly introduce concepts in music and code to newcomers. Seven 10-20 minute exercises are now available in the program to introduce new users to the power of code in music.

--- oOo ---

Please keep the feedback coming and support the project by reviewing Manhattan, liking the videos on YouTube, etc. If this release is well-received, the next will be Release Candidate 1 - but working on custom instruments / samples and multiple patterns is also in the works!

notes.title: Now available in Early Access + Playtest!
notes.content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z4zlU0SMAuc
I'm delighted to announce the release of both the Early Access (v1.9.24, stable) and Playtest (v2.0 beta, mostly stable) versions of Manhattan! Free to download and use on Steam.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43334362/46beb7a53383c8e007a639eb941498eafe00ab0c.gif⠀

Manhattan v2 Beta (Playtest version) includes:

High definition graphics - a completely reworked UI supporting scalable graphics with Retina and High DPI support, including a new DirectX hardware-accelerated graphics engine on PC.
Horizontal Mode - prefer to think laterally literally? Switch between the default vertical timeline of trackers, or horizontal timeline of conventional DAWs.
New waveform and piano roll visualisations - make beautiful music, make music beautiful. Press $ on your keyboard or the status bar to cycle between edit mode and mesmorising visualisations of the patterns and processes your music.
Improved DAW plugin support - use Manhattan in your creative process, as a VST/AU instrument inside your favourite music tools. Windows version introduces a dual-window approach; pattern overview in the host, pattern editing in a separate, maximisiable window. Developed using REAPER, but tested in a handful of other hosts - please feedback experiences with yours!
New font and light/dark UI theme - select the scheme that suits your eyes (or time of day) - white-on-black (Dark mode) or ink-on-paper (Light mode) - with Manhattan's new 'handwritten' take on the classic DOS font.
Native support for Apple Silicon - now a Universal Binary, Manhattan takes advantage of the CPU and GPU features of M1, etc., while continuing to support Intel and older machines. Please feedback on graphics performance for your machine - Apple changed a lot in recent macOS versions.
Over 100 other improvements across workflow, graphics, UI, audio, MIDI import, help documentation, and more.

So please download/update, tell your friends, and let me know how you get on!
